description: Last-resort fallback for a real user mistake (cp_loss >= 50) with a clear better_move but NO shape / NO principle / NO firing R-rule. Severity tier respects [[cp-loss-is-not-material]] — never translate cp_loss to 'X pawns lost'. When the V5 curriculum walker, blocked_pawn detector, or board_state_describer produced a fact (Mohit 2026-05-21), prefer the named-curriculum / named-principle / board-state variant so the caption is coach-voice teaching instead of bare engine-speak ('X was better'). Asymmetric threshold: the bare engine-speak default variant requires cp_loss >= 100, but detector-driven variants fire at the lower promotion threshold (50). Curriculum deviation has the highest variant priority — when user deviated from a curated opening tree, the tree's hand-authored wrong_feedback is the best teaching we have.

fact_glossary.severity_phrase: Authored phrase picked from severity_phrases via severity_tiers
fact_glossary.curriculum_deviation_clause: Hand-authored wrong_feedback from opening_curriculum.json — surfaced by V5 when the user deviated from a curated opening tree. Highest variant priority.
fact_glossary.curriculum_expected_move: Book-theory move the tree expected (used as backup display).
fact_glossary.curriculum_opening_name: Matched opening's name (used as backup display).
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_file: File letter of a user pawn whose advance was blocked by the played piece move. Set by principle_blocked_pawn detector — names an opening principle violation.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_square: Target square the blocked pawn would have advanced to.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_would_support: Central pawn square the blocked pawn would have supported diagonally. When set, the with_blocked_pawn_supports variant teaches the specific structural reason; otherwise with_blocked_pawn names the principle generically.
fact_glossary.board_state_clause: Pre-rendered string from board_state_describer (1-3 facts joined). Lower priority than blocked_pawn and curriculum.

variants.with_blocked_pawn_supports: {move_san} {severity_phrase} — it blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn. {best_move} would have supported your {blocked_pawn_would_support} pawn.
variants.with_blocked_pawn: {move_san} {severity_phrase} — it blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn from advancing to {blocked_pawn_square}. {best_move} was better.
